result.note: Tests the September 2026 New Zealand legislation implementing the India trade deal and the small share of India's exports it covers.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–New Zealand trade deal as of September 2026:
items: New Zealand's parliament passed legislation implementing the deal, zeroing tariffs on qualifying Indian goods.
New Zealand accounts for more than 1% of India's exports.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because New Zealand takes only 0.13% of India's exports. The implementing law passed on 17 September 2026 and removes tariffs on qualifying Indian goods, though the market it opens is small.
questions.source: New Zealand's parliament passed legislation implementing its India trade deal, zeroing tariffs on qualifying Indian goods, though the market is small at 0.13% of India's exports.
